Only one face model is enrolled. Lightin: Only one face model is enrolled. Lighting changes how your face looks to the camera, so a single model can fail in the evening under lamps (or in daylight). Add a second model recorded in different light to keep unlocking reliable at any time of day.

Ubuntu Hello will scan your face twice:: Ubuntu Hello will scan your face twice: once now, and once more in different lighting (for example evening lamps instead of daylight), so it recognises you reliably at any time of day. Press Scan to record the first model.
Your first model is saved, so face login: Your first model is saved, so face login already works. The room must still be bright enough to see your face — change the light rather than turning it off — then try again, or skip and add a model later from Settings.
First model saved. Now change the light: First model saved. Now change the light — for example turn a lamp on or off, move away from the window, or use the other room light — keep your face clearly visible, then press Scan again.
Look at the camera you selected: an infr: Look at the camera you selected: an infrared camera shows a small light that blinks while Ubuntu Hello tests it. This tells us whether it can see your face in the dark.
